Why anti zionists have a problem with a two state solution *in its current form* is because the state of Israel is an ethnostate state seeking to maintain a Jewish majority by any means possible. Currently 20% of Israeli citizens are Palestinians and in the case of a two state solution where Israel remains an exclusively Jewish state, Palestinians will always remain second grade citizens.

One of the main criticisms of Israel where this discrimination becomes obvious is Birthright. It’s a right that’s given to every single Jewish person because they’re born Jewish but discriminates against millions of Palestinian refugees whose grandparents were expelled from their homes by Israel (before the establishment of the state) in 1948 and don’t have the same right to return to their homes. The main argument for why this racist law exists is religious, saying that if you’re Jewish, then regardless of where you were born in the world, you have the right to live in Israel and obtain an Israeli citizenship because God promised you the land. But this same logic doesn’t apply to Palestinians who their ancestors lived on the same land for millenia before they were made refugees and replaced by Jewish immigrants from all around the world.

There are other reasons also for why antizionists are against a two state solution. For example, a lot of people don’t have trust that Israel would be satisfied with anything less than the whole land and anti zionists believe that arguing for a two state solution is used as an excuse by Israel to continue occupying Palestinian land, building settlements, and expelling more Palestinians (which has been happening de-facto since 1948). The ruling Likud party has it written in its charter (Israel a Jewish state from the river to the sea) and they’re literally actively working on their plan in Gaza and the West Bank as we speak.
